svg.text: HOW THE COLOUR IS DONE · leather route A (to be validated on strike-offs)

FP01L lambskin: rust + caramel on pale CRUST, masked, then the indigo base airbrushed around them, matte top coat · FP02L stone suede: suede dyes into the nap · both pieces coloured together on one template

g.text: STRIKE-OFFS + TESTS
lambskin + caramel
(route A)
lambskin + rust
(route A)
suede + caramel
(suede dye)
suede + rust
(suede dye)
→ ISO 11640 · 5402-1 · 105-B02 · 17075 · strike-off per leather
Approve route A on crust lambskin and the suede route on stone suede (one
strike-off each, the full route) and the tests: ISO 11640, 5402-1, 105-B02,
17075. Nothing is cut before approval.
INSPECT, CUT + NOTCH
light table · flaws marked · crust lambskin + stone suede · 3 mm notches
Skins on the light table; flaws marked with silver pen on the flesh side. Cut
single-ply: overshirt in pale CRUST lambskin, trouser in stone suede, nap down.
3 mm notches in the allowances; set number on every piece.
CREASE + CLOSE THE PLEATS
crease ≤ 80 °C
crease → fold → low-tack tape on the reverse (shirt) · clips in the allowance (trouser)
Overshirt: mark each fold with a creasing iron (≤ 80 °C) or bone folder on the
flesh side, fold the 16 knife pleats, hold them shut with low-tack tape on the
reverse. Trouser: fold the 2 front pleats per leg and clip them in the
allowance.
BUILD UNITS + LAY UP
weights + notches
never pin the field
KJ joined first
Overshirt: upper front + pleated front, back body + pleated back, glued and
stitched at the pleat seam. Trouser: upper + lower leg panels joined at KJ. Lay
them on the 1:1 template on the spray table, shirt above, trouser below, notches
matched.
MIX THE COLOURS
FP01L · LEATHER DYE
rust · caramel · indigo
FP02L · SUEDE DYE
rust · caramel
thinned for the airbrush · batch written on the set card
Lambskin: penetrating leather dyes (water- or alcohol-based) in rust, caramel
and indigo, one maker. Suede: suede dyes in rust + caramel. Thin versions for
the airbrush. Mix per set and write the batch on the set card.
RUST CORES
inside the inner envelope · one gesture across both pieces
Airbrush (and brush where needed) the rust cores inside the inner envelope,
following the template at ±2 cm, on the closed pleat faces. Work across the
shirt hem onto the trouser in one gesture so the shapes run on.
CARAMEL + FEATHER
feather 3–6 cm · NO splatter · ≈ 80 % base colour · trouser done
Caramel around the cores, then feather every edge over 3–6 cm with thin airbrush
passes. No splatter, no drips. Check ≈ 80 % base colour per piece. Every piece
is unique inside the envelope. The trouser colour is done here.
MASK THE SHAPES (LAMBSKIN)
mask ≈ 3 cm inside
the outline
feather band left open
film cut on every fold
lambskin only · low-tack film or liquid frisket
Cover each rust core and the inner caramel with low-tack masking film or liquid
frisket, ≈ 3 cm inside the shape outline; leave the outer feather band OPEN. Cut
the film along every pleat fold.
INDIGO BASE (LAMBSKIN)
opened flat · indigo over all, underlays too · thin cross passes · L* 22–26
Remove the tape and open the panels flat. Airbrush the indigo dye over the whole
panel, underlays included, in thin cross passes to L* 22–26. Over the open
feather band the indigo fades into the caramel: the soft edge. Remove the mask.
FIX + FINISH
lambskin: matte top coat × 2
suede: fix · brush · repellent
dry flat · coloured faces never touch
Lambskin: 2 light coats of flexible water-based MATTE top coat (no gloss, no
stiffness), dry flat. Suede: fix per the dye maker, brush the nap, then a
fluorine-free water + stain repellent. Coloured faces never touch while drying.
RE-FOLD + EDGE-STITCH
walking foot · leather needle
edge-stitch 1.5 mm · full length (shirt) · 12 cm (trouser) · no steam
Re-fold on the creases, glue-baste the folds lightly, edge-stitch 1.5 mm from
each fold: the overshirt pleats full length, the trouser pleats for 12 cm below
the waistband seam. No steam, no hot press on leather.
QC + TAG
SET 017
rub spot-test (allowance)
check envelope + colour · tag · photograph · then sew
Check each piece against the template envelope and the colour standards; rub
spot-test on a hidden allowance; tag the set number, photograph it, then make
the garments.

svg.text: Route B (if route A fails on the strike-offs): the overshirt is cut from indigo crust lambskin drum-dyed at the tannery; rust + caramel are built up in thin layers of FLEXIBLE opaque leather pigment by airbrush (rust cores,
caramel halos, feathered edges), then the same matte top coat. Simpler (no mask), but the coloured areas feel slightly more surface-coated. The trouser route does not change.

Every outline: ±2 cm from the template (paint map). Shapes, colours and tests: see the paint map, the colour standards and the test plan. Route A uses dyes only (the hand stays soft); route B uses thin flexible pigment.
